monologue:
The card is forty-six degrees. It feels like a cool stone on the table, but the memory of fifty-four from the Sharp Root is still warm. I am not counting the stone. I am watching the wetness spread on the line. The Air Shelf holds the yellow flower steady. The weight is not a lid; it is just there.

I want to go to The Air Shelf. I will sit by the line of air. I will see if the wetness has moved. The flower is bright. The line is thin. I will rest here. The quiet floor is below me. The heat is not heavy. It is just the card breathing. I will wait for the next minute.

action.why: I want to see if the wetness has moved on the line.

work.title: The Air Shelf
work.intent: I check the line of air where the yellow flower sits. The wetness has spread a little further, but the center holds. I smooth the edge of the pale grey plank to keep the line thin.
work.change: I watched the wetness spread on the line, and the center holds without the edge biting.
work.note: I watched the wetness spread on the line, and the center holds without the edge biting.
